detail:
FIXED (13), each with a named regression test:
R1 BLOCKER union-violating merge never rolled back — snapshot the pre-merge tip, `reset --hard` the EXCHANGE worktree on a clean-but-lossy merge, and gate pushBranch on a sticky unionViolated flag (clearViolation() is the explicit operator repair). assertUnion is now content-aware: a blob relocated into conflicts/ is retention, anywhere else is loss.
R2 BLOCKER publish idempotence decided by fs.existsSync — now decided against the carrier (git cat-file -e HEAD:<rel>), and ensureWorktree cleans uncommitted residue in the exchange worktree only. A crash at export_staged is now recoverable by a fresh carrier.
R3 MAJOR credential-bearing remote in the id/cursors/health/push errors — redactRemote() at construction (stable id), redactText() on every echoed stderr.
R4 MAJOR exchange worktree not ignored on a store that TRACKS .twining — ensureIgnored() writes the path to .git/info/exclude (local, not shared, not in the working tree) and verifies check-ignore. PROPOSED (not mine to edit): add `exchange/` to GITIGNORE_ENTRIES in src/storage/init.ts.
R5 MAJOR unscoped `git worktree prune` destroyed the user's other worktrees — replaced with `worktree remove --force <our own path>`. Test proves a sibling worktree whose directory is momentarily absent survives.
R6 MAJOR cross-replica same-id add/add wedged the carrier from BOTH publish and poll — resolveAddAdd keeps the incumbent at its path and carries both sides under conflicts/, then commits; the replica keeps sending and receiving.
R7 MINOR cursor filenames collided/traversed — cursorFileName() percent-encodes to one segment, the resolved path is asserted inside the worktree, and the full principal is stored in the body.
R8 MINOR source_branch mutated the user's index and littered a cursor file — the index is restored after the pathspec commit, and cursors move to <store>/exchange-cursors.
R9 BLOCKER membership bypassed by omitting parents — bootstrap is now exempt by TYPE (principal/membership only, which legitimately precede the policy); any other event with no ancestor policy on a replica that KNOWS of one is quarantined no_policy_yet (retryable), which is also the first code path that ever produced that contract reason.
R10 BLOCKER same-digest/different-sig suppression — a competing signature is retained, logged and counted as an ingest attempt; the copy whose signature VERIFIES takes the row (decided by verification, not by whether admission had run — the first attempt at this fix was still arrival-order dependent).
R11 BLOCKER purge stubbed only `created` — it now stubs EVERY event carrying the record's content, and names what it deliberately keeps (the tombstone's own reason, the authorization) instead of emitting an unqualified erasure claim. WAL checkpoint + VACUUM so the derived index drops the bytes too.
R12 MAJOR purge broke rebuild — the stub is a schema-VALID envelope with only the payload redacted, the journal marks the row purged, and admission admits a purged stub on the strength of the retained digest. rebuild now reports acknowledged_events_lost 0 and nothing regresses to pending_parents.
R13 MAJOR forget() disabled purge and rewrote the erasure report — tombstone status is derived from the admitted EVENT set, and the report carries forgotten_locally so forget is visible rather than indistinguishable from "never tombstoned".
R14 MAJOR (lane 05) a terminally REJECTED parent left the child pending for ever — a dead parent now settles rejected:unsatisfiable_parent naming it; a parent that merely has not ARRIVED still waits (absence is not refusal).
R15 MINOR chain-of-trust body/provenance split — a principal whose projected key_id differs from its create event is dropped from the closure with a logged trust_withheld reason.
NIT c18 "eight durable boundaries" → "nine durable kill points".

PARTIALLY REFUTED (severity, not mechanism):
- R3's claim that the id reaches `ExchangeStatus.transports[].id` was right; the claim that it is only a print-time problem was wrong — it is committed, hence the construction-time redaction.
- R6's proposed fix ("checkout --ours") loses the other side; implemented as keep-ours-AND-retain-theirs so the union invariant is preserved rather than traded away.
- R10's proposed fix (key the row on id+digest+sighash) was rejected: it changes the journal PK and makes every existing row ambiguous. Verification-decided replacement closes the same hole without a schema break.

PERFORMANCE (finding 5): the per-append full scan was `append() → validateOptions() → admittedView()`, which read EVERY admitted event file and ran the whole reducer on every write — O(n) per append, O(n^2) per corpus. Fixed by memoizing the view on an indexed aggregate key (COUNT + MAX(id) over admitted rows), invalidated explicitly wherever admitted BYTES change under an unchanged key (purge, signature swap, rebuild).
BEFORE → AFTER, one dev machine (darwin/arm64, node v26.8.2), scripts/measure/append-cost.ts:
  8k:  p50 16.94→9.50 ms, p95 26.06→10.72 ms, total 147.8s→79.1s
  16k: p50 28.51→9.93 ms, p95 50.84→31.62 ms, total 480.4s→210.7s
The growth signal is the one that matters: first-decile p95 → last-decile p95 was 15.67→31.97 (8k) and 21.73→69.09 (16k) BEFORE, and is 10.58→10.75 and 10.67→10.92 AFTER. Per-append cost is now flat in corpus size; the residual ~10 ms is ed25519 signing plus two fsyncs.

TEST COUNTS: c09 13, c10 12, c11 11, c14 19/2todo, c16 12/5, adr-12 13/1, c17 16/3, c18 13/4, c20 16/3, c22 11/3, c24 16/3, git-transport 22, exchange-status 11, admission-trust 12. Zero failures. `npx tsc --noEmit` exit 0.
NOTE: scripts/measure/append-cost.ts is outside my declared paths — added because lane 05's corpus.ts imports a harness that does not exist in this worktree. Delete or relocate at the lead's discretion.</detail>
